cars.generation: Third-generation Z31 original single-turbo V6 road sports family
cars.variant: 300ZX Turbo two-seater — 1986 USA range brochure, five-speed
cars.specification_market: Original Nissan 1986 Cars and Trucks USA range brochure, nine PDF spreads; all rendered and 300ZX spread PDF6 (printed 10–11) read individually. Selected Turbo two-seater with five-speed overdrive manual, not normally aspirated 2-seater, 2+2, later facelift, 200ZR or Z32 twin turbo. The brochure states 3.0-litre OHC V6, fuel injection, adjustable damping and 16-inch Turbo wheels. It prints no road output or exact displacement in this spread: none is invented. Its approximately 215-mph GTP race-car remark is not a road-car top speed. Optional leather/electronics are not declared standard.
cars.summary: The Z31 300ZX marked the Z-car line’s transition from inline-six power to the turbocharged VG V6. Its aerodynamic sports-car body and new engine architecture made it a distinct engineering chapter in the enduring Z lineage, preceding the separately developed Z32.

Full file 183 pages; first 16-page contact sheet and base PDF1–7/9/11 individually read. Actual swept capacity is 1997.4 cc; 3395.6 cc is the 1.7 turbo-equivalence result, not physical displacement. The index suffix (1997) is not the car’s model year. No rally output, maximum allowed rebore, later evolution extension, automatic or later V6 VR-4 is imported. cars.summary: The original Galant VR-4 combined turbocharged twin-cam power, four-wheel drive and four-wheel steering in a road saloon that became Mitsubishi’s Group A rally platform. Its competition derivatives earned six WRC victories and helped develop the four-wheel-drive technology subsequently used by the Lancer Evolution programme.

cars.generation: Original 1300 four-speed Bertone-designed mid-engine road sports family
cars.variant: X1/9 1300 — 1977 Fiat Motors of North America brochure
cars.specification_market: Original Fiat Motors of North America two-page sales brochure hosted as 1977. Both pages rendered; full technical PDF2 visually read. Selected original 1290-cc US four-speed carburetted road car with 8.5:1 compression. No unprinted output is invented or borrowed from the factory retrospective’s European 75-CV account. California catalyst/final-drive alternatives are not silently universal. Later 1498-cc Five Speed, injected Bertone, Dallara Group 5 and Abarth prototype data are excluded.
cars.summary: The X1/9 made a transverse mid-engine layout, four-wheel independent suspension and four disc brakes accessible in a compact production sports car. Marcello Gandini’s Bertone wedge body and removable Targa roof gave it a lasting design identity, with particularly strong success in the American sports-car market.

cars.generation: Original 1998-cc sixteen-valve Dolomite Sprint road saloon family
cars.variant: Dolomite Sprint — January 1974 base recognition, four-speed
cars.specification_market: Original British Leyland/Triumph/RAC FIA 5542 Group 1 base production form, cover valid from 1 January 1974. Complete file 51 pages; first 16-page contact sheet and base PDF1/8–12/14 read individually. Retains 1998 cc and explicitly declared 127 net BHP at 5700 rpm without adding a DIN/SAE conversion. Optional Laycock overdrive, alternate ratios, subsequent automatic, Group 2 racing and 1854-cc eight-valve Dolomite form 5477 are excluded. Recognition date is not substituted for original public launch.
cars.summary: The Dolomite Sprint brought an ingenious single-overhead-cam, sixteen-valve engine to a refined compact sporting saloon. Contemporary first-hand assessment placed its performance alongside the Escort RS1600 while highlighting its quieter, better-appointed road character, making it a significant British high-performance saloon rather than an ordinary Dolomite.
